title: I made a free game engine that runs entirely in your browser — build, play & share worlds with friends (RUMPUS ENGINE)
author: Jarred-Smith
selftext:
**RUMPUS ENGINE — build it, break it, share it.**

RUMPUS ENGINE is a free game studio that runs entirely in your browser. No download, no install, no account — open the link and you're either playing someone's world or building your own. It works on desktop, phones, and with a controller.

**WHAT IT IS**

A complete build-and-play loop in one tab. Open the editor, shape a world — terrain, water, lighting, physics props, even scripted cutscenes — press DEPLOY, and you're playing it. Share it as a link and anyone who clicks is standing inside your level seconds later.

**WHY IT'S DIFFERENT**

• Zero friction. The entire engine ships as a single web page. If you can open a link, you can play — and if you can play, you can build.

• Not just a shooter. The same editor makes first-person shooters, racing games (sketch your track by hand and the engine builds it), top-down twin-stick arenas, 2.5D side-scrollers, and weapon-free puzzle/adventure levels.

• Real multiplayer, no servers to rent. Peer-to-peer co-op, duels, free-for-all, team deathmatch, king of the hill, and full multiplayer racing. A live "Open games" list means joining is one tap — no codes to text around.

• Bring the internet's 3D models with you. Search Poly Pizza and Sketchfab from inside the editor and drop models straight into your world. Rigged characters get automatic animation retargeting, with a joint editor to fix the quirky ones.

• Depth where it counts. Weapon loadouts with attachments that genuinely change play (scopes magnify, extended mags hold more, suppressors shrink the radius enemies hear your shots). Enemy AI that hunts by sight and sound. Racing with AI rivals, ghost laps, and starting grids.

• A community that ships. Browse the built-in level library, play anything instantly, open any level in the editor to see how it was made and remix it — or submit your own for review, no account required.

**FEATURES AT A GLANCE**

• In-browser world editor: props, primitives, terrain & floor painting, water zones, lights, skies (real HDR), cinematic camera tools

• 8 objective types: eliminate, survival, extraction, defend, destroy, escort, puzzle, race

• Campaign builder — chain levels into a full game and export it as a single file

• Multiplayer: co-op waves, 1v1 duel, FFA, TDM, KOTH, racing — with a live lobby browser

• Custom characters and enemies from any rigged GLB model

• Weapon attachment system with real gameplay effects

• Mobile-first touch controls that adapt to the level type, plus full gamepad support

• Community level library with one-click play and in-game submission

• 100% free, built on open-source (three.js, Rapier physics)



Play now: [https://www.rumpusengine.com](https://www.rumpusengine.com)

replies.author: Jarred-Smith
replies.body:
lol, I started building it a few months ago on a whim. It really started out as a test to see if Claude could build a FPS and then it just kind of snowballed from there. I built it entirely by myself (with some major input and suggestions from my 14 year old son who gave me amazing insight into what game builders and gamers would want in an engine). I’ve always wanted to build games and spent so much time learning Unity back in the day. It, and Unreal, are so bulky and require huge PC specs, plus a fairly deep knowledge for coding, that they seem inaccessible to the general population that may only have a phone or cheap computer. Throughout the build of Rumpus, I constantly made sure it was optimized and had options for users on low end devices to still be able to use it smoothly. 

The demo reel doesn’t quite do the full system justice. There’s a lot going on under the hood. I’m particularly proud of the cinematic builder which could also be used to create browser based movies, pre-vis for movie planning, etc. 

As far as what did I use to build it, I used Claude Code and a mix of Opus 4.8 and Fable 5. The entire game engine is a single html file around 2.5MB. I used three.js and rapier physics engine, plus APIs for sketchfab and poly pizza for the models. Poly haven is used for the materials, and freesounds is used for the audio api.

Please, build, test it, break it, and let me know how it goes!

comments.author: RBRND
comments.body:
It's awesome!  
Some small nitpicks:   
\- I can't rebind controls to my extra mouse buttons.  
\- When playing Deploy, I sometimes missclick on the set of bonus (that we are provided after finishing a wave) because it appears just in front my cursor.  
\- Ennemies don't make any sound indicator, which helps them get behind our back quite easily

replies.author: Jarred-Smith
replies.body: Good feedback! I can easily add binding controls for the mouse. Those bonus options are customizable and can be toggled on or off in the editor. Enemies by default don’t make any sound, but in the editor you can build out robust enemies with different types, custom models, animations, and sound effects. The default level with the primitive capsules is really a placeholder for the user to use as a foundation in their game build. Or delete and build a whole level from scratch!
